papers_read.title_as_printed: Temporal constrained joint nonnegative matrix factorization for imaging genomic study of early mild cognitive impairment (Deng et al., Neurocomputing 653 (2025) 131121)
Longitudinal study of early mild cognitive impairment via similarity-constrained group learning and self-attention based SBi-LSTM (Lei et al., Knowledge-Based Systems 254 (2022) 109466)

what_each_reports.P-68: Imaging-genetics matrix factorisation (TCJNMF) of 4-timepoint sMRI AAL ROIs plus blood DNA methylation in ADNI, 91 EMCI vs 62 NC. Ablation classifier on the mined top features, 5-fold CV: LR accuracy 0.830, AUC 0.927; RF accuracy 0.715, AUC 0.731 (Table 3). No latent class model, no pMCI vs sMCI task, no 84% figure.
what_each_reports.P-71: Similarity-constrained group sparse rs-fMRI connectivity network + self-attention stacked Bi-LSTM, baseline and year-1 rs-fMRI, ADNI-2 (102) and ADNI-3 (51), LOOCV. EMCI vs NC fused ADNI-2&3: accuracy 86.11%, AUC 93.90 (Table 4); ADNI-2 alone 87.50%; LMCI vs NC 91.42%; EMCI vs LMCI 89.42%. No pMCI vs sMCI task and no 81% figure.

quantity_a: Cross-validated EMCI vs NC discrimination of LR/RF classifiers built on TCJNMF-selected sMRI ROI + DNA-methylation features (ADNI, n=153, 5-fold CV); this is an ablation for a biomarker-mining method, not a proposed diagnostic model.
quantity_b: LOOCV EMCI vs NC (also LMCI vs NC, EMCI vs LMCI) discrimination of a Bi-LSTM on two-timepoint rs-fMRI functional connectivity networks (ADNI-2/3, n=153 incl. 46 LMCI).
incompatible_if_same: No. Even taking the nearest comparable figures (EMCI vs NC), P-68 reports accuracy 0.830 / AUC 0.927 and P-71 reports 86.11% / AUC 93.90: the same direction and practically the same magnitude. The record's 84% vs 81% pMCI/sMCI contrast appears in neither paper.

gates.task: mismatch against the record: the record states pMCI vs sMCI conversion prediction, but both papers classify EMCI vs NC cross-sectional status (P-71 also LMCI tasks). Between the two papers the task (EMCI vs NC detection) matches.
gates.dataset_family: match: both ADNI (P-68 ADNI GO/2 with DNA methylation; P-71 ADNI-2 and ADNI-3 rs-fMRI).
gates.validation_tier: match: both internal cross-validation only (5-fold vs LOOCV).
gates.modality_family: mismatch: P-68 structural MRI + blood DNA methylation; P-71 resting-state functional MRI.

endpoint_and_metric: compatible metric types (accuracy, AUC) for EMCI vs NC, but the predictor sets differ (sMRI ROI + methylation vs rs-fMRI connectivity).
performance_validity: flag does not apply: neither headline value reaches 0.97 accuracy/AUC; not in any case a disagreement.
independence: Distinct author groups. Both draw on ADNI, so some participants may overlap; not determinable from the papers.
grounds: The record's claims misread both papers: P-68 contains no latent class model and no pMCI vs sMCI prediction, and P-71 contains no 81% pMCI vs sMCI result.
Both papers actually report EMCI vs NC discrimination in ADNI, and the nearest figures (P-68 LR accuracy 0.830, AUC 0.927; P-71 86.11%, AUC 93.90) agree in direction and magnitude.
Neither paper makes a claim the other refutes; there is no disagreement to adjudicate.

record_defects: claim_a 'LCM (latent class model) achieves 84% for pMCI vs sMCI prediction on ADNI N=186': P-68 is a TCJNMF imaging-genetics study of EMCI vs NC (N=153); no latent class model, no conversion task, no 84%.

claim_b 'LSTM on same cohort achieves 81% on identical task': P-71's SSBi-LSTM uses a different ADNI rs-fMRI sample for EMCI vs NC and reports 86.11% (fused) or 87.50% (ADNI-2); no 81% pMCI/sMCI result.
resolution_note's 'LCM is probabilistic ... LSTM is deterministic' describes methods neither paper uses as stated.
The bridging-evidence papers listed are unrelated headline scores and do not explain any disagreement.
what_would_change_the_verdict: Nothing in these two PDFs; if the record intended different papers (an LCM pMCI/sMCI study and an LSTM study on one cohort), those papers would need to be identified and read.
